newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close higher on lingering crop fears.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close higher on lingering crop fears.

text.p: Spot March FCOJ futures closed slighty firmer while the back months went out sharply higher for the second consecutive session, lifted by ongoing fears of freeze damage and technically-driven buying.
The March contract closed up 0.25 cent to 93.75 cents a lb, traded 99.00 to 91.00. The back months settled 4.35 to 1.75 higher.
Floor sources said fund and trade buying gave the market an initial boost and carried the back months up the daily 5.00-cent limit.
Trade selling at the highs knocked the contracts off the highs by the close.
Even after finishing the daily limit higher across the board Monday, the market remained oversold before today's opening call, analysts said.

PaineWebber analyst Bernard Savaiko said today's gains reflected an attempt for the back contracts to catch up with yesterday's gains made in March, which is allowed to move 10.00 cents during the session.
The contract closed up 10.00 cents Monday.

On the fundamental front, players continue to await news on damage from the freeze in Florida earlier this month. The Florida Department of Agriculture puts losses to the state's citrus crop at $60 million, but there is no official tally of the damage, a spokesman for the department said.
Concern that cold temperatures forecast to hit Florida this weekend could increase prior freeze damage may have contributed to firmer prices, some market sources said.
Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said temperatures should remain in the mid 30s (degrees Fahrenheit), well above the level that would allow fruit to freeze.
